purpose: Shot list for the Lens photo benchmark (Pit Board act5). Each example is an openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photo, checked for watermarks.

shots.label: aluminum-can
shots.shoot: An empty drink can, standing up.
shots.how: Stand it on the kitchen counter. Shoot from the side at can height so the shape and the ring pull both show.
shots.avoid: Crushing it first. A crushed can is a different photo.

example.file_title: File:Can of Diet Sierra Mist lemon-lime soda, 2011.jpg
example.author: DimiTalen
example.credit: Photo: DimiTalen, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Full, unopened branded soda can on driftwood; brand label printed on the object.

shots.label: steel-tin-can
shots.shoot: An empty food can (soup, beans, tomatoes), label on or off.
shots.how: Rinse it, stand it up, shoot from slightly above so the rim shows. Holding it in your hand is fine.
shots.avoid: A lid still hanging off by a sharp edge. Press it in first.

example.author: Hockeytown11
example.credit: Photo: Hockeytown11, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Hand holding an unopened can of baked beans in a home kitchen (own work, CC0). Branded label on the can; not empty.

shots.label: aerosol-can-empty
shots.shoot: An empty spray can (air freshener, cooking spray, deodorant).
shots.how: Upright, cap on, on a counter or shelf. Fill the frame top to bottom.
shots.avoid: Pressing the nozzle to check it is empty while you shoot.

example.author: Nave do Conhecimento
example.credit: Photo: Nave do Conhecimento, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Branded insect-freeze aerosol can on a shelf; label on the object.

shots.label: scrap-metal
shots.shoot: A piece of scrap metal: an old pipe, bracket, hinge, a pan without its handle.
shots.how: Lay it on the garage floor or a workbench. One piece, or a few of the same kind.
shots.avoid: A mixed pile of metal and other junk.

example.author: W.carter
example.credit: Photo: W.carter, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Close-up of assorted rusty steel pipes.

shots.label: plastic-bottle-pet
shots.shoot: A clear plastic water or soda bottle (#1 PET), cap on.
shots.how: Stand it up against a plain wall. Clear plastic hides against busy backgrounds.
shots.avoid: A window behind it: the bottle disappears into the light.

example.author: Jiafei Slay Queen
example.credit: Photo: Jiafei Slay Queen, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Plain clear PET water bottle, no label, dark studio-like backdrop.

shots.label: plastic-jug-hdpe
shots.shoot: A milk or juice jug (#2 HDPE), rinsed.
shots.how: Side view with the handle visible. The kitchen counter is fine.
shots.avoid: Showing only the bottom with the recycling number.

example.author: Kelapstick
example.credit: Photo: Kelapstick, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Plain white square HDPE milk jug; license is PD-user (no CC URL), linked to the Commons template.

shots.label: plastic-bag-film
shots.shoot: A plastic shopping bag.
shots.how: Lay it flat on a dark table so its edges show, or hold it up by the handles.
shots.avoid: A bag stuffed inside another bag.

example.file_title: File:White plastic bag on brown wooden table.jpg
example.author: 999real
example.credit: Photo: 999real, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Plain white plastic carrier bag on a table.

shots.label: styrofoam-foam-ps
shots.shoot: A foam cup, tray or packing block (#6 polystyrene).
shots.how: On a dark surface: white foam vanishes on a white counter.
shots.avoid: Crumbs of foam everywhere. One piece, whole or broken.

example.file_title: File:Physical weathering styrofoam cup Lake Michigan obverse.jpg
example.author: Visviva
example.credit: Photo: Visviva, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Weathered foam cup found on a beach; printed cup design, partly broken.

shots.label: yogurt-container-pp
shots.shoot: A yogurt cup or tub (#5 PP).
shots.how: Empty and rinsed, lid on or beside it. Shoot at a slight angle so the depth shows.
shots.avoid: Shooting it on a store shelf among many others (the example does; yours should not).

example.author: RaffiKojian
example.credit: Photo: RaffiKojian, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Large branded yogurt tub photographed on a supermarket shelf; other tubs in background.

shots.label: cardboard-clean-dry
shots.shoot: A clean, dry cardboard box.
shots.how: A shipping box on the floor or held in one hand. Tape on is fine.
shots.avoid: Your name and address on the shipping label. Peel it off or turn the box around.

example.author: Anjaniy
example.credit: Photo: Anjaniy, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Hand holding a shipping carton; retailer logo printed on box and a courier label with barcode/handwriting on it.

shots.label: newspaper
shots.shoot: A newspaper, or a small stack of them.
shots.how: Folded, on a table. A stack is fine if it is only newspaper.
shots.avoid: Mixing in magazines or mail.

example.author: Ka23 13
example.credit: Photo: Ka23 13, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Bundled stacks of folded (Japanese) newspapers; not a single folded paper.

shots.label: pizza-box-clean-top-half
shots.shoot: A pizza box, the clean top half if you have one.
shots.how: Closed, from above, on the counter or floor.
shots.avoid: An open box full of leftovers (that is organics, not this shot).

example.author: Mike Licht from Washington, DC, USA
example.credit: Photo: Mike Licht from Washington, DC, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Closed pizza box lying on asphalt; printed joke text on the lid is part of the box.

shots.label: paper-coffee-cup
shots.shoot: A disposable paper coffee cup, lid on.
shots.how: Stand it on a table and shoot from the side at cup height.
shots.avoid: A reusable mug: it is a different item.

example.author: Henry Söderlund
example.credit: Photo: Henry Söderlund, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Paper coffee cup with printed cartoon face sleeve and plastic lid.

shots.label: glass-bottle-clear
shots.shoot: A clear glass bottle.
shots.how: Upright against a plain wall, like the PET bottle. A label is fine.
shots.avoid: A bottle with a drink still in it.

example.file_title: File:Clear glass bottle with cork stopper is displayed on a wooden surface near a window in soft natural light.jpg
example.author: Shixart1985
example.credit: Photo: Shixart1985, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Plain unbranded clear glass bottle with cork. Uploader Shixart1985 (own work, CC BY 2.0) has an AI-style description; image itself looks like a normal photo. Alternative if preferred: File:VictoriaGin bottle 750ml.jpg (CC0, branded).

shots.label: glass-food-jar
shots.shoot: A glass food jar (jam, pickles, pasta sauce), lid on.
shots.how: On the counter, at a slight angle so the lid and the glass both show.
shots.avoid: A plastic jar that looks like glass. Tap it if unsure.

example.author: Witia
example.credit: Photo: Witia, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Glass jar of home pickles with printed red lid, on a wooden table.

shots.label: ceramics-pottery
shots.shoot: A ceramic mug or plate.
shots.how: One mug on a table, handle to the side.
shots.avoid: A glass mug: ceramics are the point of this shot.

example.author: Henning Makholm
example.credit: Photo: Henning Makholm, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Plain white ceramic mug with coffee on a wooden table; PD-user-en (no CC URL).

shots.label: smartphone
shots.shoot: A smartphone, screen off.
shots.how: Lay it on a plain table, screen up, at a slight angle.
shots.avoid: A lit screen showing messages, photos or notifications.

example.author: Douglas Perkins
example.credit: Photo: Douglas Perkins, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: White Samsung Galaxy Note 4 lying on a white table.

shots.label: laptop-notebook-computer
shots.shoot: A laptop, lid open.
shots.how: On a desk, shot from the front and a little above.
shots.avoid: Anything personal on the screen. Close apps or turn it off.

example.file_title: File:Laptop, Small notebook, Netbook, Rostov-on-Don, Russia.jpg
example.author: Vyacheslav Argenberg
example.credit: Photo: Vyacheslav Argenberg, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: HP netbook on a patterned tablecloth, with a mouse and lens cap beside it.

shots.label: keyboard-mouse
shots.shoot: A computer keyboard, a mouse, or both.
shots.how: From above on the desk, the whole keyboard in frame.
shots.avoid: Cutting off one end of the keyboard.

example.author: Samiknoov
example.credit: Photo: Samiknoov, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Black keyboard on a wooden desk, shot from above.

shots.label: charging-cables-cords
shots.shoot: A charging cable, coiled.
shots.how: Coil it loosely on a table so both connectors show.
shots.avoid: A tangle of several cables (a bundle is a different shot).

example.author: ArnoldReinhold
example.credit: Photo: ArnoldReinhold, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Coiled white USB-C cable on a grey surface (file is about a faulty cable; not visible).

shots.label: alkaline-battery-aa-aaa-9v
shots.shoot: AA or AAA alkaline batteries (a few).
shots.how: Two to four batteries on a table, labels up. The example shows rechargeable AAs: same framing; the printed label is what tells them apart.
shots.avoid: Batteries still inside a remote or toy.

example.author: RAIL P (RAIL.PHOTOGRAPHY)
example.credit: Photo: RAIL P (RAIL.PHOTOGRAPHY), CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Four IKEA LADDA rechargeable AA NiMH cells (rechargeable, not alkaline).

shots.label: button-coin-cell
shots.shoot: A coin cell (CR2032 or similar).
shots.how: Get close: it is small. Tap the screen to focus and keep it in the middle of the frame.
shots.avoid: Shooting from far away, where it becomes a dot.

example.author: I G
example.credit: Photo: I G, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Single coin cell on a wooden table (model not legible; looks CR20xx-size).

shots.label: car-battery-lead-acid
shots.shoot: A car battery.
shots.how: In the garage, from the front and a little above so the terminals show.
shots.avoid: Touching both terminals, or moving the battery only to take a photo.

example.author: Shaddack
example.credit: Photo: Shaddack, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: 40 Ah lead-acid car battery, top-side view; PD-self (no CC URL).

shots.label: power-tool-battery
shots.shoot: A power-tool battery pack (drill, trimmer).
shots.how: Off the tool, on a workbench, label side up.
shots.avoid: Leaving it on the tool: then it is a drill.

example.author: Retired electrician
example.credit: Photo: Retired electrician, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: 18V power-tool battery pack on white background (file describes it as a counterfeit Ryobi; branding printed on pack).

shots.label: paint-latex-water-based
shots.shoot: A can of paint.
shots.how: Lid on, on the garage floor, from above at an angle so the lid and label both show.
shots.avoid: Opening a can just for the photo.

example.author: Ionenlaser
example.credit: Photo: Ionenlaser, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Open tin of white paint with a brush across it, top-down.

shots.label: category:hazardous
shots.shoot: A household cleaner in its bottle (spray, bleach, drain cleaner).
shots.how: Upright on the counter or under the sink, label facing the camera.
shots.avoid: Opening or mixing cleaners. Never pour one into another.

example.file_title: File:Window cleaner and an empty spray bottle.jpg
example.author: Corn cheese
example.credit: Photo: Corn cheese, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Two spray bottles (empty + window cleaner) on a kitchen counter.

shots.label: fluorescent-bulb-cfl
shots.shoot: A compact fluorescent bulb (the curly or folded-tube kind).
shots.how: Switched off, on a table, lying down or standing on its base.
shots.avoid: A broken bulb. If one breaks, air out the room and skip this shot.

example.author: Levente Fulop from Brno, Czech Republic
example.credit: Photo: Levente Fulop from Brno, Czech Republic, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Lit yellow CFL against a dark blue backdrop (studio-style, but a real photo).

shots.label: motor-oil
shots.shoot: A motor oil bottle.
shots.how: Cap on, upright on the garage floor or a shelf.
shots.avoid: Oil dripping down the outside. Wipe the bottle first.

example.author: Interiot (retouched by Where next Columbus? and H Padleckas)
example.credit: Photo: Interiot (retouched by Where next Columbus? and H Padleckas), Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Motor-oil bottle with the brand blocked out, plus a glass of oil; PD-self (no CC URL).

shots.label: clothing-wearable
shots.shoot: A piece of clothing someone could still wear (T-shirt, sweater).
shots.how: Folded, or laid flat on a bed or table, filling the frame.
shots.avoid: Your feet or legs in the shot (the example has them; yours should not).

example.author: EdaBojci
example.credit: Photo: EdaBojci, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Layered T-shirt laid flat on a table (not folded); the photographer's legs/feet are visible at the bottom.

shots.label: shoes
shots.shoot: A pair of shoes.
shots.how: Side by side on the floor, from the side and a little above.
shots.avoid: One shoe on a foot.

example.file_title: File:Worn-out torn shabby hole-ridden grey canvas shoes light soles dirty used broken laces Utgåtte slitte hullete fillete grå tøysko med lette grå plastsåler såler brukte skitne ødelagte skolisser Norway 2025 IMG 1793.jpg
example.author: Wolfmann
example.credit: Photo: Wolfmann, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Pair of worn, torn canvas sneakers on a white surface.

shots.label: textiles-fabric-scraps
shots.shoot: Fabric scraps or rags.
shots.how: A small pile on a table.
shots.avoid: Clothes that still work: those are shot 29.

example.author: Leslie Seaton from Seattle, WA, USA
example.credit: Photo: Leslie Seaton from Seattle, WA, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Basket of fabric scraps next to a box of pin cushions.

shots.label: food-scraps-organics
shots.shoot: Food scraps: peels, cores, coffee grounds.
shots.how: In a bowl or compost bin, from above.
shots.avoid: Packaging mixed into the scraps.

example.author: Benitronne
example.credit: Photo: Benitronne, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Compost bucket of vegetable and fruit peels outdoors.

shots.label: category:organics
shots.shoot: A piece of plain wood: an offcut, a plank, a pallet slat.
shots.how: On the floor, the whole piece in frame.
shots.avoid: Painted or treated wood (that has a different answer).

example.author: JohnnyEnglish1234
example.credit: Photo: JohnnyEnglish1234, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Single pine board offcut on a concrete floor; a handwritten name is on the board.

shots.label: tires
shots.shoot: A car tire.
shots.how: Lying flat or leaning against a wall, the whole tire in frame.
shots.avoid: A tire still on the car.

example.author: dave_7 from Lethbridge, Canada
example.credit: Photo: dave_7 from Lethbridge, Canada, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Single bare tire lying on gravel; this one is a small/utility-size tire, not obviously a car tire.

shots.label: category:rubber
shots.shoot: A garden hose.
shots.how: Loosely coiled on the ground.
shots.avoid: A hose on its reel: the reel becomes the subject.

example.author: www.Pixel.la Free Stock Photos
example.credit: Photo: www.Pixel.la Free Stock Photos, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Garden hose lying loose on a concrete floor (Pixel.la free-stock upload, CC0).

shots.label: mattress
shots.shoot: A mattress.
shots.how: Leaning against a wall, the whole mattress in frame. Step back.
shots.avoid: Shooting only a corner.

example.author: Eric Fischer
example.credit: Photo: Eric Fischer, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Mattress propped against a street waste container.

shots.label: category:bulky-goods
shots.shoot: A big piece of furniture: an armchair, sofa or desk chair.
shots.how: The whole piece, from a few steps back.
shots.avoid: People sitting on it.

example.author: Fumikas Sagisavas
example.credit: Photo: Fumikas Sagisavas, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Abandoned upholstered armchair under a tree (the title says sofa; it is a single-seat chair).

shots.label: aluminum-can
shots.shoot: BLURRY: the drink can from shot 01.
shots.how: Move the phone as you press the shutter. The can is still the only thing in the frame, just smeared.
shots.avoid: A different object. The label stays aluminum-can, so it has to be a can.

example.author: Big Slosh
example.credit: Photo: Big Slosh, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Real home snapshot of a walking kitten with strong motion blur. It is not a can, but it clearly shows motion blur.

shots.label: alkaline-battery-aa-aaa-9v
shots.shoot: DARK: the AA batteries from shot 21.
shots.how: Same framing as shot 21, in a dim room, flash off.
shots.avoid: Pure black. Dim, not dark.

example.author: Raita Futo from Tokyo, Japan
example.credit: Photo: Raita Futo from Tokyo, Japan, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Dark, underexposed shot of small flowers; shows low light, not a battery.

shots.label: smartphone
shots.shoot: CLUTTERED: your phone in a messy drawer or on a messy desk.
shots.how: Put the phone somewhere busy (junk drawer, crowded desk) and shoot it where it lies, roughly in the middle of the frame.
shots.avoid: Letters, papers or screens that can be read.

example.author: Yinan Chen
example.credit: Photo: Yinan Chen, Public Domain, via Wikimedia Commons
example.note: Very cluttered home-office desk (printer, papers, bottles, bowls). It is a messy desk, not a junk drawer. HDR-looking processing. Source: goodfreephotos.com, cc-pd.
